headline: Adopted a curb-cut zoning ordinance, voted 6-5 to suspend the Flock Safety camera system, approved special legislation for Vincent Fernandez, and Rourke resigned.
summary: The Council adopted a zoning ordinance expanding curb cuts, voted 6-5 to suspend the Flock Safety camera system pending a policy review, and approved an 8-year contract with Lowell Management Group, a $142,409 BHOAP grant, and a $51,225 Edward Byrne Justice Assistance Grant. It referred a tenant rights ordinance to the Housing Subcommittee, defeated a change to the fall meeting schedule, and accepted several utility and resident requests for referral to department review.
decisions: Adopted an ordinance amending zoning rules for curb cuts, 11 yeas.
Referred National Grid's request to install two 4-inch conduits on South Highland Street near Gorham Street to the Wire Inspector.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains on Aiken Street and Avenue, Dalton Street and Court, and Exeter Street to the Wire Inspector.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace 55 feet of gas main at 47 Fulton Street to the Wire Inspector.
Referred a request to purchase and place outdoor exercise equipment at Fr. Maquire Park to the City Manager.
Referred a request for the City Manager to advocate for 24-hour shelter services and state property access for Lowell's Winter Protocol Program to the City Manager.
Referred a request to explore commemorating the Portuguese community's contributions in the Back Central neighborhood to the City Manager.
Adopted a request for the City Manager to suspend use of the Flock Safety system pending a policy review, 6 yeas to 5 nays.
Withdrew a motion requesting maintenance and upkeep of Olga Nieves Park after the issue was resolved.
Referred a request to reassess safety at Dublin and Adams Streets intersection, including a possible 4-way stop, to the City Manager.
Referred a request to repair a damaged fence at the STEM Academy to the City Manager.
Referred a request for the Commissioner of Public Works to report on winter weather and snowstorm preparations to the City Manager.
Referred a request for the City Manager, City Clerk, and City Auditor to prepare a list of 2027 goals by end of October.
Referred a request to clarify that canvasser and solicitor regulations do not apply to political canvassing to the City Manager.
Referred a request for a report on DOJ's presence and activities in Lowell during the 9/1/26 election to the City Manager.
Referred a request for the Law Department to draft a zoning amendment increasing setback requirements due to the ADU law to the City Manager.
Referred a request to explore installing a bench at the reservoir on the Reservoir Street side to the City Manager.
Referred a request for an updated fire hydrant operational inventory report to the City Manager.
Referred a request for a corrective action plan for the walkway in front of 715 Lakeview Avenue to Ennell Street to the City Manager.
Referred a request for a list of alternatives to Flock that don't share data to any database to the City Manager.
Referred a request for a list of all expired board members to the City Manager.
Referred a request for an updated accident report since new signals were installed on Westford Street at Stedman Street to the City Manager.
Adopted a request to ask the federal delegation to award Sergeant Major Dors 'Gene' Musgray the Congressional Medal of Honor, 11 yeas.
Adopted approval of out-of-state travel for the LPD, 11 yeas.
Adopted acceptance of a $1000 gift from the Conant Family, 11 yeas.
Adopted acceptance and expenditure of a $142,409 BHOAP Grant, 11 yeas.
Adopted acceptance and expenditure of a $51,225 FY26 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant, 11 yeas.
Defeated a motion to amend the October, November, and December 2026 Council meeting schedule, 6 yeas to 5 nays, for not meeting the two-thirds threshold.
Adopted authorization for the City Manager to execute an 8-year contract with Lowell Management Group, Inc., 11 yeas.
Adopted authorization for the City Manager to execute a contract with Passport Labs, Inc., 11 yeas.
Adopted authorization for the City Manager to file special legislation for Vincent Fernandez, 10 yeas to 1 nay.
Withdrew a vote to transfer $43,000 for salaries.
Referred an ordinance amending Chapter 176 on Tenant Rights and Housing Stability Notification to the Housing Subcommittee after its first reading.
Continued the Neighborhoods Subcommittee report of September 15, 2026 to the next meeting.
Accepted and adopted orders for National Grid's utility pole request at 26 Caddell Avenue and Boston Gas's gas main replacement on Middlesex Street from Maude Street to Saunders Street.
Referred a property damage claim to the Law Department for report and recommendation.
Referred Edward 'Bud' Caulfield's request regarding motorized scooters and bicycles to the City Manager and Law Department for report and recommendation.
Referred Mary Avelino's request to remove a handicap parking sign at 19 Washington Street to the Transportation Engineer for report and recommendation.
Referred Boston Gas's request to relocate a gas main on Stockbridge Avenue to a public hearing on October 6, 2026.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains along Lawrence and Woburn Streets to a public hearing on October 6, 2026.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains on Leroy, Canal, and Grove Streets to a public hearing on October 6, 2026.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains on Llewellyen, Beacon, Third, and Bennett Streets to a public hearing on October 6, 2026.

4. GENERAL PUBLIC HEARINGS (Scheduled for 7PM)
4.1. Ordinance - Amend Zoning - Curb Cuts.
In City Council, Given second reading, hearing held.  Motion to adopt by C. 
Scott, seconded by C. Rourke.  Adopted per Roll Call vote 11 yeas (C. 
Chau, C. Descoteaux, C. Juran, M. Gitschier, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. 
Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. Rourke, C. Scott).  So voted.  Motion by
C. Robinson, seconded by C. Scott to take Item #7.4 here for discussion.  
So voted.  C. Juran questioned the benefit of wider curb cuts and noted the
Planning Board discussion indicating that there would be an effect on street
parking.  Manager Golden, Jr. noted the issue and indicated the ordinance 
came about through Council request.  C. Scott noted the cuts differed from 
district to district and that was unfair.  C. Robinson noted goal to put their 
cars on their property as it will assist with work that would be done on the 
road.  C. McDonough commented on the issue with curb cuts and parking.

the neighborhood.  C. Mercier commented on the effort of the Portuguese
people to develop that area.

usage, the company's use of data, and the audit process of the data.
In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager.  Adopted per

Nuon, C. Scott), 5 nays (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, C. Mercier, C. Robinson, 
C. Rourke).  So voted.  Registered speakers, Ron Peacetree (commented – 
noted his expertise and favored the technology but it needs oversight) and

Tina Degree (commented – violated peoples’ rights and that there are many 
violations), addressed the Council.  Motion by C. Mercier, seconded by C. 
Nuon to suspend rule and allow Ken Seagal and Emily Gertanmak to 
address the body.  So voted.  Mr. Seagal noted the importance of the 
equipment to combat crime and that any violations are over exaggerated.  
Ms. Gertanmak noted issue is with the sharing of data.  C. Scott noted the 
support of the use of cameras; however, the issue would be the sharing of 
data with other agencies and that suspending use while policies are 
updated would be proper.  C. Nuon noted benefit of the system when used 
correctly.  C. Juran questioned the process to suspend use of the camera.  
Manager Golden, Jr. Indicated that policies and answer to questions are 
being worked on currently and that suspending use of the system would not
be beneficial.  C. Juran noted prior direction to bring matter into an 
executive session.  C. Robinson was not supportive of the use of the 
camera even though it was a valuable tool that is only has good as the 
policies developed.  C. Robinson noted issues could be worked out while 
system is still in use.  C. Rourke noted that the LPD Superintendent 
indicated that the use of the camera was effective and necessary.  C. Chau 
noted it was a balance between safety and privacy and that more 
information is needed.  Chair was relinquished to Vice Chair Nuon at 9:06 
PM.  M. Gitschier noted an executive session was needed and that it 
should not be shut down with no alternative.  Manager Golden, Jr. noted his
conversations with the Superintendent and that matters are being 
addressed while system is still in operation.  Chair returned at 9:11 PM.  C. 
Scott questioned how an audit of the data is done.  Manager Golden, Jr. 
outlined the process and how department handles request for data.  C. 
Nuon noted a balance was needed and that an executive session would 
provide necessary information.  C. Scott supported discussion in executive 
session.  C. McDonough did not support the use of the camera as there are
other tools with less risk.  C. Rourke noted suspension of the system would 
lead to bad consequences.

make a request to our federal delegation to award Sergeant Major 
Dors "Gene" Musgray the United States Congressional Medal of

In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager. Adopted per 
Roll Call vote 11 yeas (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, C. Juran, M. Gitschier, C.
